items.plain: God taught me that words are not true because they are eloquent, nor false because they are clumsy. Wisdom and folly are like healthy and unhealthy food, and either can be served in a plain dish or a fine one.
items.core_idea: Truth does not depend on eloquent or plain speech

items.plain: I lied to my mother and slipped away by night while she wept and prayed I would not sail. God, who forgave me, refused her request so as to grant what she always truly wanted for me.
items.core_idea: God denied a mother's plea to grant her deeper wish

items.plain: I liked to think some other nature sinned in me, not I; it flattered my pride to be blameless. But it was wholly I, and refusing to see myself as a sinner made my sin harder to heal.
items.core_idea: Refusing to own your sin makes it harder to heal

items.plain: O God, my hope since youth, where were you? You made me wiser than the beasts, yet I walked in darkness, looked for you outside myself, and despaired of ever finding truth.
items.core_idea: I searched outside myself for God and despaired

items.plain: I kept my heart from agreeing to anything, afraid of falling headlong, but hanging in that suspense hurt me even more.
items.core_idea: Refusing to commit out of fear did more harm

items.plain: Like someone burned by a bad doctor who fears trusting a good one, my soul could only be healed by believing, yet refused the cure, O God, for fear of believing something false.
items.core_idea: Past deception made me afraid to trust real healing

items.plain: As I thought these things over, God, you were with me: when I sighed you heard me, when I wavered you guided me, and when I wandered the world's broad road you did not abandon me.
items.core_idea: God stayed with me through all my wandering

items.plain: I longed for honours, money and marriage, and God laughed at me. Chasing them brought bitter pain, and the kinder God was, the less he let anything but himself taste sweet to me.
items.core_idea: God let nothing but himself satisfy me

items.plain: In Milan I saw a beggar, merry on a few coins, while I toiled anxiously through ambition toward the same passing joy. His joy was not true, but mine was even less so; he was carefree, I full of fear.
items.core_idea: Ambition brought me less joy than a carefree beggar

items.plain: Life is empty and death's hour unknown. If it comes suddenly, in what state will we leave, where will we learn what we neglected here, and will we not be punished for that neglect?
items.core_idea: Death may come suddenly; do not neglect your soul

items.plain: Torn this way and that, I kept putting off turning to the Lord, while dying a little inside each day. I wanted a happy life but feared it where it truly lived, fleeing it while seeking it.
items.core_idea: I kept delaying the very happiness I sought

items.plain: When the woman I lived with was sent away for my marriage, my heart bled. She vowed herself to God; I, a slave to lust, took another. The wound did not heal; the pain dulled but grew hopeless.
items.core_idea: Lust kept my wound from healing

items.plain: Praise to you, God, fountain of mercy. As I grew more miserable, you came nearer, ready to pull me from the mire, though I did not know it. Only fear of death and judgment held me back.
items.core_idea: As I sank lower, God drew nearer

items.plain: How crooked the paths of a soul that leaves God hoping for something better! It turns every way and finds only pain, for God alone is rest. Yet God rescues us and promises to carry us home.
items.core_idea: God alone is rest, and he carries us home

items.plain: Why fear what does not exist? If we fear for nothing, the fear itself is the evil, tormenting the soul, and it is all the worse because there is nothing to fear and we fear anyway.
items.core_idea: Needless fear is itself an evil

items.plain: O God, my heart groaned in anguish and you heard, though I did not know it; my silent sorrow was a loud cry to your mercy. You alone knew my suffering; words could not carry it to friends.
items.core_idea: God heard the anguish no friend could hear

items.plain: Lord, you are eternal but not forever angry; you pity our frailty. With inner prodding you kept me uneasy until I saw you, and through healthy sorrows you slowly healed my pride and the dim sight of my mind.
items.core_idea: God heals us through uneasy, healthy sorrows

items.plain: Urged to return to myself, I went inward with God as my guide and helper, and with my soul's eye I saw, above my mind, the unchanging Light.
items.core_idea: Turning inward, I saw God's unchanging Light

items.plain: O God, you are Truth that is Eternity, Love that is Truth, and Eternity that is Love. You are my God, and I long for you night and day.
items.core_idea: God is Truth, Love and Eternity, my constant longing

items.plain: It is good for me to hold fast to God, because if I do not remain in him I cannot remain in myself, while he, remaining in himself, makes all things new.
items.core_idea: Without holding to God, I cannot hold myself together

items.plain: When God quietly soothed me and closed my eyes to empty things, my old self loosened and my frenzy calmed. I woke in God and saw him as infinite, in a sight not from the body.
items.core_idea: Calmed by God, I woke and saw him infinite

items.plain: I marvelled that I now loved God and not an illusion. Yet I did not hold on: God's beauty drew me up, and my own weight, the habit of the flesh, dragged me back down in sorrow.
items.core_idea: God's beauty lifts me; old habit drags me down

items.plain: It is one thing to see the land of peace from a mountaintop and find no way there, attacked on impassable paths; it is another to walk the road that leads there, guarded by heaven's army.
items.core_idea: Seeing peace differs from walking the road to it

items.plain: I was now sure of God's eternal life, though I saw it dimly, and no longer wanted more certainty, only more steadfastness. But my everyday life was unsteady, and my heart still needed cleansing of the old ways.
items.core_idea: I needed steadfastness more than certainty

items.plain: I had found the precious pearl I should have sold everything to buy, and still I hesitated.
items.core_idea: Having found the treasure, I still hesitated

items.plain: A commander's triumph is sweeter the harder the battle; sailors rejoice most after a storm that nearly drowned them; a friend's recovery brings more joy than his health ever did.
items.core_idea: Joy is greater after danger and struggle

items.plain: Everywhere, the greater joy is introduced by the greater pain.
items.core_idea: Greater joy follows greater pain

items.plain: How high God is in the heights and how deep in the depths! God never leaves, yet we hardly ever return to him.
items.core_idea: God never leaves; we rarely return

items.plain: Rise up, Lord, and act: stir us, call us back, set us alight and draw us; become sweet to us, so that we may love and run to you.
items.core_idea: A prayer for God to stir us to love

items.plain: My will was chained: wrong desire became lust, lust indulged became habit, and habit unresisted became necessity. My new will to serve God could not yet beat the old, and the two fought in me and tore my soul apart.
items.core_idea: Desire becomes habit, and habit becomes a chain

items.plain: Weighed down by the world, I was held as in pleasant sleep. Like someone who knows it is time to rise but lingers in bed, I knew giving myself to God's love was better, yet desire held me.
items.core_idea: Knowing what is better, I lingered like a sleeper

items.plain: When God showed me the truth, I had only drowsy answers: soon, in a moment, just a little longer. But my soon never came, and my little while went on and on, as sin held me captive.
items.core_idea: My "soon" never came

items.plain: As Pontitianus spoke, God turned me to face the self I had kept behind my back, so I would see how foul and crooked I was. Horrified, I could not escape myself. I had known it but pretended not to.
items.core_idea: God made me face the self I avoided

items.plain: As a youth I had begged God for chastity, saying: give me chastity and self-control, only not yet. I feared God would answer quickly and cure a desire I wanted satisfied, not ended.
items.core_idea: I prayed for purity, but not yet

items.plain: I lashed my soul with every argument to make it follow God, but it drew back. All reasons were spent; only a silent shrinking remained, dreading to be cut off from the habit that was killing it.
items.core_idea: The soul clings to the habit that kills it

items.plain: The mind commands the body and it obeys at once; the mind commands itself and meets resistance. It tells the hand to move and it does, yet when it tells itself to will, it does not.
items.core_idea: The body obeys the mind; the mind resists itself

items.plain: When I was deciding to serve God, it was I who willed and I who refused. I neither fully willed nor fully refused, so I was at war with myself and torn apart by myself.
items.core_idea: Half-willing, I was torn apart by myself

items.plain: When eternity draws us upward and earthly pleasure holds us down, it is one soul that wills neither fully, and so it is torn, putting truth first in thought but not setting habit aside.
items.core_idea: A divided will knows truth but keeps old habits

items.plain: I cried out in sorrow: how long, how long, tomorrow and tomorrow? Why not now? Why not end my impurity this very hour?
items.core_idea: Why not change now, not tomorrow?

items.plain: How sweet it suddenly became to do without those trifling pleasures! What I had feared to lose, I now gladly gave up.
items.core_idea: Letting go of what I feared losing became joy

items.plain: Wherever that resting place is, my dear friend Nebridius lives there as God's child, drinking wisdom from God's fountain as much as he thirsts, endlessly happy. I think he remembers me, since God, whom he drinks, remembers us.
items.core_idea: My dead friend lives happily in God and remembers me

items.plain: My good things were no longer outside me. Those who seek joy from outside soon grow empty, wasting themselves on passing, visible things, and in their hunger lick at mere shadows.
items.core_idea: Seeking joy outside leaves you feeding on shadows

items.plain: God, you are always the same and never change; in you is a rest that forgets all toil. We need not chase the many things that are not you, for you alone, Lord, have made me live in hope.
items.core_idea: In unchanging God is rest from all toil

items.plain: How I wept at your hymns, God, deeply moved by the sweet voices of the Church! The voices flowed into my ears, truth seeped into my heart, my devotion overflowed in tears, and I was happy.
items.core_idea: Sacred song moved me to happy tears

items.plain: Just as flattering friends lead us astray, critical enemies usually set us right.
items.core_idea: Critics correct us; flatterers corrupt us

items.plain: God made my mother a peacemaker: hearing bitter words from both sides of a quarrel, she repeated only what would reconcile them. Many instead pass on angry words and add more; kindness means quenching ill will, not feeding it.
items.core_idea: Repeat only words that heal a quarrel

items.plain: We said: if every noise of body and world fell silent, even the soul's own thoughts, and God alone spoke directly, not through anything made, and that moment of understanding lasted forever, would that not be entering your Master's joy?
items.core_idea: If all fell silent, God alone would speak

items.plain: What hurt me so deeply inside, except a fresh wound from the sudden tearing away of our sweet and dear habit of living together?
items.core_idea: Grief is the wound of a shared life torn away

items.plain: I was upset that these human events, which must come to pass in the natural order, had such power over me, and so I grieved over my grief and was worn down by a double sorrow.
items.core_idea: Grieving over my grief doubled my sorrow

items.plain: I confess to you, Father of the fatherless, that I bathed and felt no different, for the bitterness of sorrow would not leave my heart. Then I slept, woke, and found my grief somewhat softened, and remembered verses by Ambrose.
items.core_idea: Sleep softened a grief nothing else could

items.plain: God, maker and ruler of all, clothes the day in light and pours gentle sleep over the night, so that tired bodies regain strength for work, sinking hearts are lifted, and sorrows are eased.
items.core_idea: God gives sleep to restore strength and ease sorrow

items.plain: I let the tears I had held back flow as much as they wanted, and my heart rested on them, finding peace, because they were heard by you, God, not by people who would have mocked my weeping.
items.core_idea: My heart found rest in tears before God

items.plain: The things of this life that we grieve most deserve grief least, and the things that deserve grief most are the ones people grieve least.
items.core_idea: We grieve most what matters least

items.plain: Why should people hear my confessions, as if they could heal my weaknesses? They are a race eager to know others' lives and lazy about fixing their own.
items.core_idea: People pry into others' lives but neglect their own

items.plain: Hearing of past sins God has forgiven wakes the heart from despair and its "I cannot", rousing it to trust God's mercy, where the weak grow strong by knowing their weakness. Good people rejoice that those evils are past.
items.core_idea: Stories of forgiven sins wake hope instead of despair

items.plain: When I love my God I do not love bodily beauty, light, music, perfume, food or embrace. Yet I love an inner light, music, fragrance, food and embrace that space, time, breath, eating and fullness cannot take away.
items.core_idea: Loving God is an inner, unfading delight

items.plain: I asked the earth, sea, air, sun, moon and stars whether they were my God. All said they were not. When I asked them to tell me of him, they cried out loudly: he made us.
items.core_idea: All creation says: we are not God; he made us

items.plain: Memory is vast, God, a boundless room no one has sounded, yet it is mine, and I cannot grasp all that I am. People travel to marvel at mountains, seas and stars, and pass themselves by without wonder.
items.core_idea: We marvel at mountains but pass ourselves by

items.plain: I can remember past joy without feeling joyful, past sorrow without sorrow, past fear without fear, and past desire without desire. Sometimes I even recall old sorrow with joy, and old joy with sorrow.
items.core_idea: We can recall feelings without feeling them again

items.plain: Ask two men if they want to go to war: one says yes, the other no. Ask if they want to be happy: both say yes at once, and each chooses for that same reason.
items.core_idea: Everyone wants happiness, though they seek it differently

items.plain: I have met many people who would deceive others, but no one who wants to be deceived.
items.core_idea: Many deceive, but no one wants to be deceived

items.plain: People love truth when it shines on them and hate it when it rebukes them. Wanting not to be deceived, yet wanting to deceive, they love truth when it reveals itself and hate it when it reveals them.
items.core_idea: We love truth until it exposes us

items.plain: O Truth, you answer all who ask, clearly, though not all hear clearly or hear what they want. Your best servant does not seek to hear what he wants, but wants what he hears from you.
items.core_idea: Want what God says, not what you wish

items.plain: I loved you too late, God, Beauty ancient and ever new! You were within and I searched outside. You called and broke my deafness, shone and ended my blindness; you touched me, and I burned for your peace.
items.core_idea: God was within me while I searched outside

items.plain: Is not human life one long trial? No one wants troubles; God asks us to endure them, not love them. In hard times I long for good ones; in good times I fear hard ones. Where is the middle?
items.core_idea: Life is trial: we crave good times and fear bad

items.plain: Self-restraint gathers us into one after we were scattered among many things. Whoever loves anything alongside God not for God's sake loves God too little. O love that burns and never consumes, my God, set me alight.
items.core_idea: Love nothing beside God that is not loved for God

items.plain: No one should feel safe in this life, which is all trial: whoever could be made better from worse can also become worse from better. Our only hope and sure promise is God's mercy.
items.core_idea: No one is safe from falling; trust only God's mercy

items.plain: Lord my God, listen, look, have mercy and heal me; before you I have become a puzzle to myself, and that is my weakness.
items.core_idea: Before God I have become a puzzle to myself

items.plain: At home, a lizard catching flies or a spider trapping them often grabs my attention. I may then praise God the Creator, but that is not what first draws me. Rising quickly is one thing; not falling, another.
items.core_idea: Recovering quickly differs from not falling at all

items.plain: God, you know how far you have changed me: first healing my urge to justify myself, so you could forgive and heal the rest. You curbed my pride and gave me your yoke; it is light, though I feared it.
items.core_idea: God's yoke proved light, though I feared it

items.plain: When someone praised for a gift God gave him enjoys the praise more than the gift, God disapproves, and the one who gives praise is better than the one praised: one delights in God's gift, the other in human approval.
items.core_idea: Value God's gift more than praise for it

items.plain: Lord, I enjoy praise, but truth more: I would rather be right and blamed by all than wrong and praised by all. Still, I wish approval did not add to my joy, yet it does, and blame lessens it.
items.core_idea: I love truth more than praise, yet praise moves me

items.plain: Our words and deeds tempt us to seek praise and others' approval. The temptation works even when I rebuke it in myself, and often takes empty pride in despising empty pride, which is then no contempt at all.
items.core_idea: Pride can boast even of despising pride

items.plain: Sometimes God lets me feel a rare inner sweetness, like a taste of the life to come. But old habits drag me back down, and I weep. Here I can stay but would not; there I would but cannot.
items.core_idea: Bad habit holds me where I would not stay

items.plain: My weaknesses are many and great, but God's medicine is stronger.
items.core_idea: God's remedy is stronger than my weaknesses

items.plain: Frightened by my sins and misery, I planned to flee to the wilderness, but God stopped and strengthened me: Christ died for all so we would live for him. Lord, I cast my care on you; teach and heal me.
items.core_idea: Instead of fleeing, I cast my cares on God

items.plain: God knows our needs before we ask, yet we pray, opening our hearts, confessing our misery and God's mercy, so God will fully free us to be happy in him, as he calls us to be humble, merciful and pure.
items.core_idea: We pray to open our hearts, not to inform God

items.plain: Lord my God, light and strength of the blind and the weak, and of the seeing and the strong, hear my soul crying from the depths. If you do not hear us there, where can we go?
items.core_idea: A cry to God from the depths

items.plain: What shines through me and strikes my heart without hurting it, so that I shudder and burn? I shudder because I am unlike it, and burn because I am like it.
items.core_idea: I shudder where unlike God, burn where like
items.extended_text: What is that which gleams through me, and strikes my heart without hurting it; and I shudder and kindle? I shudder, inasmuch as I am unlike it; I kindle, inasmuch as I am like it. It is Wisdom, Wisdom's self which gleameth through me; severing my cloudiness which yet again mantles over me, fainting from it, through the darkness which for my punishment gathers upon me.

items.plain: We are saved in hope, so we wait patiently for God's promises.
items.core_idea: In hope we wait patiently for God's promises

items.plain: Answering a question is one thing; mocking the questioner is another. I would rather say "I do not know" than raise a laugh at someone asking deep things and win praise for a false answer.
items.core_idea: Better to say "I don't know" than mock a question

items.plain: God, you have made my days grow old, and they slip away, and I do not know how.
items.core_idea: My days slip away, and I don't know how

items.plain: How miserable that I do not even know what I do not know. Before you, God, I do not lie; I speak as my heart is. You will light my lamp; Lord my God, you will brighten my darkness.
items.core_idea: I don't know what I don't know; God enlightens

items.plain: Courage, my mind, keep pressing on. God is our helper; he made us, we did not make ourselves. Push on to where truth is starting to dawn.
items.core_idea: Take courage and press on toward the dawning truth

items.plain: My years are spent in mourning. You, Lord, eternal Father, are my comfort, but I am scattered among times I do not understand, my inmost thoughts torn by turmoil, until your love's fire melts me into you.
items.core_idea: Scattered by time, I long to be gathered into God

items.plain: How high God is, and yet the humble in heart are his home, for he lifts up those who are bowed down, and those he raises do not fall.
items.core_idea: The highest God dwells with the humble

items.plain: Moved by Scripture, Lord, my poor understanding is wordy, because seeking says more than finding and knocking takes more work than receiving. Yet your promise holds: ask and receive, seek and find, knock and it opens. Truth does not deceive.
items.core_idea: Seek and knock; God's promise will not deceive

items.plain: Let God, my heart's light, speak to me, not my darkness. I strayed yet still loved you, and barely heard you calling me back. Now I return, thirsting for your fountain. Living from myself was death; in you I revive.
items.core_idea: Living from myself I died; in God I revive

items.plain: How wonderfully deep are your words, God! Their surface invites even children, yet they are a marvellous depth. It is awe-inspiring to look into them, an awe of reverence and a trembling of love.
items.core_idea: Scripture's simple surface hides wondrous depth

items.plain: Lord, your judgments are fearsome, because your truth belongs to no one person but to all of us. Whoever claims as his own what you offer everyone is driven from shared truth into a private lie.
items.core_idea: Truth belongs to all; claiming it privately breeds lies

items.plain: Let us not puff ourselves up against one another, but love the Lord our God with all our heart, soul and mind, and our neighbour as ourselves.
items.core_idea: Love God fully and your neighbour as yourself

items.plain: I call on you, my God, my mercy, who made me and did not forget me when I forgot you. I call you into my soul, which you prepare for yourself through the longing you inspire in it.
items.core_idea: God remembered me when I forgot him

items.plain: We do not sink or rise in space but through our loves: love of worries drags our spirit down, and God's holiness lifts us through love of untroubled rest, toward the highest rest.
items.core_idea: Our loves sink us or lift us toward rest

items.plain: Give yourself to me, my God. I love you, and if it is too little, I want to love more. I only know I am miserable without you, and all abundance that is not my God is emptiness to me.
items.core_idea: Everything but God is emptiness to me

items.plain: Fire rises and stones fall; each is pulled by its own weight to its proper place, restless when out of place and at rest when restored. My weight is my love; wherever I am carried, love carries me there.
items.core_idea: My love is my weight; it carries me

items.plain: My God, in you I breathe a little when I pour out my soul in praise, yet my soul grows sad again. My faith answers: why are you sad, my soul? Hope in the Lord and endure until day breaks.
items.core_idea: When sad, hope in the Lord until day breaks
items.extended_text: Behold, I too say, O my God, Where art Thou? see, where Thou art! in Thee I breathe a little, when I pour out my soul by myself in the voice of joy and praise, the sound of him that keeps holy-day. And yet again it is sad, because it relapseth, and becomes a deep, or rather perceives itself still to be a deep. Unto it speaks my faith which Thou hast kindled to enlighten my feet in the night, Why art thou sad, O my soul, and why dost thou trouble me? Hope in the Lord; His word is a lanthorn unto thy feet: hope and endure, until the night, the mother of the wicked, until the wrath of the Lord, be overpast, whereof we also were once children, who were sometimes darkness, relics whereof we bear about us in our body, dead because of sin; until the day break, and the shadows fly away.

items.plain: Let us share our bread with the hungry and bring homeless poor people into our homes. Let us clothe the naked and not look down on our own kin.
items.core_idea: Feed the hungry, shelter the homeless, clothe the naked

items.plain: Do not shape yourselves to the world; hold back from it, for the soul lives by avoiding what kills it when desired. Restrain wild pride, lazy indulgence and false knowledge, so the beasts within are tamed.
items.core_idea: The soul lives by avoiding what kills it

items.plain: I know how to live with little and with plenty; in every situation I have learned to be full or hungry, to have much or go without. I can do everything through Christ, who strengthens me.
items.core_idea: Content in plenty or need, strengthened by Christ

items.plain: God taught me to tell a gift from its fruit. The gift is the thing given, such as money, food, drink, clothing, shelter or help; the fruit is the good and right will of the person giving.
items.core_idea: The giver's goodwill matters more than the gift

items.plain: Lord God, who have given us everything, give us peace: the rest of the Sabbath that has no evening. For this whole beautiful, very good world will pass away when its course is done.
items.core_idea: Pray for God's peace that has no evening

items.plain: God's foolishness is wiser than human wisdom, and God's weakness is stronger than human strength.
items.core_idea: God's weakness outdoes human strength

items.plain: Do not fool yourself. If you think you are wise by this world's standards, become a fool so that you may become truly wise.
items.core_idea: Become a fool to become truly wise

items.plain: It matters little to me if you or any human court judges me; I do not even judge myself. A clear conscience does not acquit me; the Lord judges. So judge nothing before he comes and reveals hearts.
items.core_idea: Leave judgment to the Lord, not people

items.plain: Who makes you better than anyone else? What do you have that you did not receive? And if you received it, why boast as if you had not?
items.core_idea: Everything you have was given; why boast?

items.plain: Everything is permitted to me, but not everything is helpful. Everything is permitted to me, but I will not let anything master me.
items.core_idea: Not everything allowed is good for you

items.plain: Knowledge makes people proud, but love builds them up. Anyone who thinks he knows something does not yet know as he should.
items.core_idea: Knowledge puffs up; love builds up

items.plain: In a race all runners run, but only one wins the prize, so run to win. Athletes train with strict self-control for a crown that fades; we do it for one that lasts forever.
items.core_idea: Run with discipline for a lasting prize

items.plain: If you think you stand firm, be careful not to fall. Every temptation you face is common to people. God is faithful: he will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear, and will provide a way out.
items.core_idea: God never lets temptation exceed what you can bear

items.plain: No one should look out only for themselves; each should seek the good of others.
items.core_idea: Seek others' good, not just your own

items.plain: The eye cannot tell the hand it does not need it, nor the head tell the feet. In fact, the parts of the body that seem weaker are essential.
items.core_idea: The parts that seem weakest are essential

items.plain: When one part of the body suffers, every part suffers with it; when one part is honoured, every part rejoices with it.
items.core_idea: We suffer and rejoice together

items.plain: If I speak every human and angelic language but lack love, I am just a noisy gong. With prophecy, all knowledge and mountain-moving faith but no love, I am nothing. Giving everything away without love gains me nothing.
items.core_idea: Without love, every gift is worthless

items.plain: Love is patient and kind; it does not envy, boast or act proud. It is not rude, selfish or easily angered, and keeps no record of wrongs. It delights in truth and bears, hopes and endures everything. Love never fails.
items.core_idea: Love is patient and kind, and never fails

items.plain: As a child I spoke and thought like a child; grown up, I put childish ways aside. Now we see dimly, as in a mirror, then face to face. Faith, hope and love remain, and the greatest is love.
items.core_idea: Faith, hope and love remain; love is greatest

items.plain: By God's grace I am what I am. His grace toward me was not wasted; I worked harder than all the others, yet it was not I but God's grace working with me.
items.core_idea: By God's grace I am what I am

items.plain: Do not be fooled: bad company corrupts good character.
items.core_idea: Bad company corrupts good character

items.plain: When our mortal bodies become immortal, the saying comes true: death is swallowed up in victory. Death, where is your sting? Sin is death's sting, and the law gives sin power. Thank God for victory through Jesus Christ.
items.core_idea: Through Christ, death loses its sting

items.plain: So, dear brothers and sisters, stand firm and unshakable, always giving yourselves fully to the Lord's work, knowing that your work in the Lord is never wasted.
items.core_idea: Stand firm; work for the Lord is never wasted

items.plain: Stay alert, stand firm in the faith, be brave and strong. Do everything in love.
items.core_idea: Be brave and strong, and do everything in love

items.plain: The first speaker said: how strong wine is! It leads drinkers astray, makes king and orphan, rich and poor alike, drowns sorrow and debt, turns friends to drawn swords, and afterwards they remember nothing. Is wine not strongest?
items.core_idea: Wine overpowers everyone, making them forget and err

items.plain: All the earth calls on truth and heaven blesses it. Wine, kings, women and all people are unjust and will perish, but truth stays strong forever, takes no bribes and does what is just. Blessed be the God of truth.
items.core_idea: Truth outlasts and outranks everything

items.plain: When the new temple was founded, old priests and elders who remembered the first one wept aloud, while many others shouted for joy with trumpets, so that weeping and joy could not be told apart, and the noise carried far.
items.core_idea: Weeping for the past mingled with joy for the new

items.plain: I said: Lord, I am ashamed and confused before you, for our sins are piled above our heads and our wrongs reach up to heaven, from our ancestors' time until today.
items.core_idea: Ashamed before God of sins piled high

items.plain: As the people wept on hearing the law, they were told: this day is holy to the Lord, so go and feast, send portions to those who have nothing, and do not grieve, for the Lord will bring you honour.
items.core_idea: On a holy day, feast, share and stop grieving

items.plain: If we claim to have no sin, we fool ourselves and the truth is not in us. If we confess our sins, God is faithful and just, and will forgive us and cleanse us of all wrongdoing.
items.core_idea: Confess your sins and God will forgive

items.plain: Whoever claims to be in the light but hates a brother is still in darkness. Whoever loves a brother stays in the light and does not stumble; whoever hates walks blind in darkness, not knowing where he goes.
items.core_idea: Hatred blinds; love keeps you in the light

items.plain: Do not love the world or its things; whoever loves the world lacks the Father's love. Its lusts and pride do not come from the Father. The world and its desires are passing, but whoever does God's will lives forever.
items.core_idea: The world passes; doing God's will lasts forever

items.plain: Dear children, let us not love just with words or talk, but with actions and in truth.
items.core_idea: Love in deeds, not just words

items.plain: Dear friends, let us love one another, because love comes from God; everyone who loves is born of God and knows God. Whoever does not love does not know God, because God is love.
items.core_idea: God is love, so love one another

items.plain: There is no fear in love; perfect love drives out fear, because fear has to do with punishment. Whoever is afraid has not been made perfect in love.
items.core_idea: Perfect love drives out fear

items.plain: Anyone who says "I love God" but hates his brother is a liar, for if he does not love the brother he can see, how can he love God, whom he has not seen?
items.core_idea: You cannot love God while hating others

items.plain: Dying, David told his son Solomon: I am going the way of all the earth. Be strong and act like a man; keep God's law and walk in his ways, so you prosper in all you do, wherever you go.
items.core_idea: Be strong and walk in God's ways

items.plain: Solomon prayed: Lord my God, you made me king after my father, but I am like a little child who does not know how to lead. Give me an understanding heart to judge your people and tell good from evil.
items.core_idea: Ask God for an understanding heart

items.plain: My father David longed to build a house for God's name. God told him it was good that he had it in his heart, but he would not build it; his son would.
items.core_idea: A good intention honoured, though another fulfils it

items.plain: King Rehoboam asked his father's old advisers how to answer the people. They said: if you serve these people today and speak kindly to them, they will serve you forever.
items.core_idea: Serve people kindly and they will follow you

items.plain: A widow told Elijah she had only enough flour and oil for a last meal before she and her son died. He said: do not fear; feed me first, for God says your flour and oil will last until rain.
items.core_idea: Do not fear; give first, and God will provide

items.plain: Elijah asked the people: how long will you keep wavering between two sides? If the Lord is God, follow him; if Baal is, follow Baal. The people said nothing.
items.core_idea: Stop wavering; choose whom you will follow

items.plain: God passed by: a mighty wind tore the mountains and smashed rocks, but God was not in the wind. Nor was God in the earthquake that followed, nor in the fire. After the fire came a still, small voice.
items.core_idea: God came not in the storm but quietly

items.plain: The messenger urged Micaiah to agree with the other prophets and tell the king good news. Micaiah answered: as the Lord lives, I will say whatever the Lord tells me.
items.core_idea: Speak what is true, not what pleases

items.plain: Do not fear the words of a sinful man, for his glory will end in dung and worms. Today he is raised up; tomorrow he is gone, returned to dust, and his plans have perished.
items.core_idea: Don't fear the boasting of the wicked; they pass

items.plain: Judas said: it is easy for many to be defeated by a few. To heaven it is all one to save with many or few, for victory in battle does not come from a large army; strength comes from heaven.
items.core_idea: Strength comes from heaven, not numbers

items.plain: Simon told his two eldest sons: my family and I have fought Israel's battles since youth and often won. Now I am old and you are grown; take our place and fight for our nation, and may heaven help you.
items.core_idea: The old hand on the struggle to the young

fix.display_text: And Simon called his two oldest sons, Judas and John, and said to them, I and my kindred and my father’s house have fought the battles of Israel from our youth, even to this day; and things have prospered in our hands, that we should deliver Israel oftentimes. But now I am old, and you moreover, by his mercy, are of a sufficient age: be you instead of me and my brother, and go forth and fight for our nation; but let the help which is from heaven be with you.

items.plain: All people are like grass, and all human glory like a wildflower. The grass dries up and the flower falls, but the Lord's word lasts forever.
items.core_idea: Human glory fades; God's word endures

items.plain: Let your beauty come not only from outward things like braided hair, gold jewellery or fine clothes, but from your inner self, the lasting beauty of a gentle and quiet spirit, which is very precious to God.
items.core_idea: True beauty is a gentle, quiet spirit

items.plain: Be united, compassionate, loving and courteous. Do not repay evil or insult in kind, but bless instead. Whoever wants a good life should guard their tongue, turn from evil, do good and pursue peace, for the Lord watches the righteous.
items.core_idea: Repay insult with blessing and pursue peace

items.plain: Above all, love each other deeply, because love covers many sins. Welcome one another without complaining. Use whatever gift you have received to serve others, as good stewards of God's many kinds of grace.
items.core_idea: Love deeply, for love covers many sins

items.plain: Dear friends, do not be surprised by the fiery trial that has come to test you, as though something strange were happening to you.
items.core_idea: Do not be surprised when trials come

items.plain: So humble yourselves under God's mighty hand, and he will lift you up in time. Throw all your worries on him, because he cares for you.
items.core_idea: Cast your worries on God; he cares for you

items.plain: After you have suffered a little while, the God of all grace, who called you to eternal glory in Christ, will himself make you complete, firm, strong and settled.
items.core_idea: After brief suffering, God will make you strong

items.plain: Hannah answered: no, my lord, I am a deeply sorrowful woman. I have not been drinking; I was pouring out my soul to the Lord. Do not think me wicked; I have been speaking out of great grief and distress.
items.core_idea: Pouring out a grieving soul to God

items.plain: Stop talking so proudly, and do not let arrogance come out of your mouth, for the Lord is a God who knows, and he weighs every action.
items.core_idea: Drop arrogance; God weighs every deed

items.plain: The Lord makes some poor and some rich; he brings low and lifts up. He raises the poor from the dust and the needy from the rubbish heap to sit with princes and inherit a seat of honour.
items.core_idea: God lifts the poor from the dust

items.plain: Samuel told the people: do not be afraid. You have done all this wrong, yet do not turn away from the Lord; serve him with all your heart. Do not chase empty things that cannot help or save you.
items.core_idea: Despite wrongdoing, don't turn from God

items.plain: Samuel said: does the Lord delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices as much as in obedience to his voice? Obeying is better than sacrifice, and listening better than the fat of rams.
items.core_idea: Obedience is better than sacrifice

items.plain: Saul told Samuel: I have sinned. I broke the Lord's command and your instructions because I was afraid of the people and did what they wanted.
items.core_idea: Fear of people led me to disobey God

items.plain: People look at outward appearance, but the Lord looks at the heart.
items.core_idea: God looks at the heart, not appearances

items.plain: The women sang that Saul had killed thousands and David tens of thousands. Saul was furious: they credit David with more than me; what is left for him but the kingdom? From that day Saul eyed David with suspicion.
items.core_idea: Envy turned Saul against David

items.plain: David bowed to the ground three times, and he and Jonathan kissed and wept together, David most of all. Jonathan said: go in peace, for we have sworn in the Lord's name that he binds us and our descendants forever.
items.core_idea: Friends part in tears, bound by a lasting vow

items.plain: Saul wept and told David: you are more righteous than I, for you repaid my evil with good. The Lord put me in your hands and you spared me. Who lets an enemy go unharmed? May the Lord reward you.
items.core_idea: David spared his enemy, repaying evil with good
